zotero papers summer.zipThis literature package contains three fundamental papers spanning neuroanatomy, signal processing, and interactive virtual paradigms. Click to expand the summaries and key BCI relevance below: Lécuyer et al. (2008) — Brain-Computer Interfaces, Virtual Reality, and Videogames Reveal Takeaways & BCI Relevance Core Focus: Navigating the intersection of BCI signal acquisition and real-time virtual environment (VE) feedback. Key Takeaways: Proves that highly immersive and interactive VR setups increase user motivation, shorten BCI calibration training, and improve signal classification rates compared to generic 2D monitors. Highlights landmark BCI game architectures, such as the MindBalance tightrope-walker game (using visual attention to two SSVEP checkerboards phase-reversed at 17 Hz and 20 Hz). Outlines design guidelines for mapping discrete BCI classifications to game commands (e.g. camera navigation, object manipulation). Lotte (2014) — A Tutorial on EEG Signal-processing Techniques for Mental-state Recognition in Brain–Computer Interfaces Reveal Takeaways & BCI Relevance Core Focus: An introductory math and engineering tutorial detailing the BCI classification pipeline (spatial filtering, band power extraction, and classification). Key Takeaways: Explains the mathematical motivation for spatial filtering (e.g. Laplacian, Bipolar, or CSP) to mitigate spatial blurring and the low SNR of raw scalp EEG. Details why BCI setups require a two-phase loop: a calibration/training phase to tune weights and thresholds using labeled data, followed by an online test/use phase. Defines the standard feature extraction method: calculating band power in the (8-12 Hz) and (16-24 Hz) ranges over the motor cortex (C3/C4) and classifying it using Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). Grèzes & Decety (2001) — Functional anatomy of execution, mental simulation, observation, and verb generation of actions: A meta-analysis Reveal Takeaways & BCI Relevance Core Focus: A structural and functional mapping of shared motor representations in the human brain during physical execution and mental simulation (motor imagery). Key Takeaways: Confirms a structural overlap in the cortical networks engaged in action execution and mental simulation (motor imagery), including the primary motor cortex (M1), dorsal/ventral premotor cortex, and SMA. Hand motor imagery specifically drives focal activations in the sensorimotor cortex hand representation area (approximately to , to ). Provides the neuroanatomical foundation for targeting (left hemisphere) and (right hemisphere) scalp electrode locations to capture contralateral SMR desynchronization during imagined right/left hand movements. Engine Unity SteamAudio (Optional; default fallback is Unity's built-in HRTF / 3D Spatial Audio)Ensure the following standard packages are installed via Window > Package Manager: XR Plugin Management (Enables VR headset detection and platform switching). OpenXR Plugin (The cross-platform industry standard for running PCVR and standalone headsets). XR Interaction Toolkit (XRI) (Provides pre-configured VR camera rigs, controllers, ray interactors, and input actions). Unity Assets: Unity Asset Store - Top Free BPM-indexed Music (Critical for Rhythm Engine Metronomes):
Incompetech (Kevin MacLeod) — High-quality instrumental loops, fully searchable by exact BPM (Beats Per Minute) and genre (CC-BY).
Free Music Archive (FMA) — Searchable royalty-free tracks, particularly under the Electronic and Beat-heavy categories. Sound Effects (SFX) & Feedback Cues:
OpenGameArt.org — Dedicated repository for game developers. Excellent for UI clicks, success/failure tones, and sound loops.
Freesound.org — Searchable community-driven database of sound clips (great for specific neurofeedback target cues).
Sonniss GDC Audio Archive — Massive, free collections of professional-grade sound design files.
https://learn.unity.com/course/create-with-vrTrial Paradigm This loop runs deterministically to capture Event-Related Desynchronization (ERD) without cognitive adaptation. Python: uv install pylsl Unity: Drop LSL.cs and your platform's native library file (e.g., lsl.dll) into your Assets/Plugins folder. using System.Collections; using UnityEngine; using LSL; public class UnityParadigmMarkerOutlet : MonoBehaviour { private StreamOutlet outlet; private string[] currentSample = new string[1]; // LSL expects samples as arrays void Start() { // Define marker stream meta-data StreamInfo streamInfo = new StreamInfo( "UnityParadigmMarkers", // Stream Name "Markers", // Stream Type (Critical for discovery) 1, // Channel Count 0, // Irregular/Event-driven sampling rate channel_format_t.cf_string, "UnityVR_RhythmRPG_001" // Unique Source ID ); outlet = new StreamOutlet(streamInfo); } // Call this method to kick off a trial loop block public void StartNewTrial() { StartCoroutine(TrialRoutine()); } private IEnumerator TrialRoutine() { // Phase 1: Fixation / Rest (with 2.0s to 3.0s jitter) SendMarker("10_REST_START"); yield return new WaitForSeconds(Random.Range(2.0f, 3.0f)); // Phase 2: Cue / Stimulus Onset (1.0s) SendMarker("20_CUE_ONSET"); yield return new WaitForSeconds(1.0f); // Phase 3: Active Rhythmic Task Execution (3.5s) SendMarker("30_TASK_START"); yield return new WaitForSeconds(3.5f); // Phase 4: Feedback Window Display (1.5s) SendMarker("40_FEEDBACK_START"); yield return new WaitForSeconds(1.5f); SendMarker("00_TRIAL_END"); } private void SendMarker(string markerValue) { currentSample[0] = markerValue; // Pushes the string marker immediately into the local network with local clock timestamp outlet.push_sample(currentSample); Debug.Log($"[LSL Sent]: {markerValue}"); } } Literature Guide > For Track A (Temporal) and Track B (Spatial) implementation theory, cross-reference Lotte (2014), Section 7.3 (Spatial Filtering) and Section 7.4 (Alternative Approaches). > For the neuroanatomical justification of choosing electrodes and , review the motor imagery meta-analysis by Grèzes & Decety (2001).Track Aimport numpy as np class TemporalFilterContract: def __init__(self, fs: int): """ fs: Sampling frequency of the EEG amplifier (e.g., 250 Hz) """ self.fs = fs def process(self, epoch: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """ Transforms raw data in the time/frequency domain. INPUT: epoch -> 2D array of shape (n_channels, n_samples) OUTPUT: filtered_epoch -> 2D array of shape (n_channels, n_samples) """ # 1. Pre-Execution Contract Validation assert isinstance(epoch, np.ndarray), "Input must be a NumPy array." assert epoch.ndim == 2, f"Input must be 2D (channels, samples). Got shape {epoch.shape}" # --- YOUR IMPLEMENTATION HERE --- # Implementation A.1: 4th-order causal Butterworth bandpass (8-30 Hz) # Implementation A.2: Local Moving Average / Basic Filter Bank Block filtered_epoch = epoch # Replace with actual logic # -------------------------------- # 2. Post-Execution Invariant Validation assert filtered_epoch.shape == epoch.shape, ( f"Dimension mismatch! Output shape {filtered_epoch.shape} " f"must match input shape {epoch.shape}" ) assert not np.isnan(filtered_epoch).any(), "Output contains NaN values. Check filter stability." return filtered_epoch Track Bimport numpy as np class SpatialFilterContract: def __init__(self, channel_mapping: dict): """ channel_mapping: Dict containing indices of required channels (e.g., {"C3": 12, "FC3": 8, "CP3": 16, "C4": 14, ...}) """ self.mapping = channel_mapping def process(self, temporal_filtered_epoch: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """ Combines physical channels linearly to output virtualized source channels. INPUT: temporal_filtered_epoch -> 2D array of shape (n_channels, n_samples) OUTPUT: spatially_filtered_epoch -> 2D array of shape (n_virtual_channels, n_samples) """ # 1. Pre-Execution Contract Validation assert isinstance(temporal_filtered_epoch, np.ndarray), "Input must be a NumPy array." assert temporal_filtered_epoch.ndim == 2, "Input must be 2D (channels, samples)." # --- YOUR IMPLEMENTATION HERE --- # Implementation B.1: Bipolar Filter (e.g., C3_bipolar = FC3 - CP3) # Implementation B.2: Laplacian Filter (e.g., C3_laplacian = 4*C3 - FC3 - C5 - C1 - CP3) spatially_filtered_epoch = temporal_filtered_epoch # Replace with actual linear combination mapping # -------------------------------- # 2. Post-Execution Invariant Validation assert spatially_filtered_epoch.ndim == 2, "Output must preserve 2D structure." assert spatially_filtered_epoch.shape[1] == temporal_filtered_epoch.shape[1], ( f"Sample length corrupted! Output length {spatially_filtered_epoch.shape[1]} " f"must match input length {temporal_filtered_epoch.shape[1]}" ) assert spatially_filtered_epoch.shape[0] < temporal_filtered_epoch.shape[0], ( f"Dimensionality reduction failure. Virtual channels ({spatially_filtered_epoch.shape[0]}) " f"must be fewer than physical channels ({temporal_filtered_epoch.shape[0]})." ) return spatially_filtered_epoch Before attempting to stream live data from an amplifier, you must verify your algorithmic logic offline using synthetic data. A mock EEG data generator has been provided in the repository.Running Local Tests Locate the test harness file: tests/test_pipeline.py Uncomment your class instantiations inside the test_pipeline_contracts() function. Run the script from your terminal: python tests/test_pipeline.py If your temporal or spatial math violates the matrix shapes or introduces NaNs, the execution will trip the contract assert statements and fail immediately. Your track is complete when this script runs with zero errors.
